record.original_question: In the spaces Rat_d and Poly_d of rational and polynomial maps of degree d with the topology of uniform convergence, is the subset of expanding maps dense? Equivalently, is every rational or polynomial map approximable by maps for which some iterate uniformly expands the spherical metric on the Julia set?

evidence.quote: The map f is expanding if P ∩ J = / . It is well-known that f is expanding iff some fixed iterate of f uniformly expands the spherical metric on the Julia set; these maps are also called hyperbolic or Axiom A.
Conjecture. The expanding maps form a dense subset of Ratd and Polyd.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\widehat{\mathbb{C}}$ denote the Riemann sphere equipped with the spherical metric. For an integer $d\geq 2$, let $\mathrm{Rat}_d$ be the space of rational maps $f:\widehat{\mathbb{C}}\to\widehat{\mathbb{C}}$ of degree $d$, and let $\mathrm{Poly}_d\subset\mathrm{Rat}_d$ be the subspace of polynomial maps of degree $d$. Endow both spaces with the topology of uniform convergence with respect to the spherical metric.

For $f\in\mathrm{Rat}_d$, let $J(f)\subset\widehat{\mathbb{C}}$ denote the Julia set of $f$ (the closure of the set of repelling periodic points), and let $P(f)$ denote the postcritical set, i.e. the closure of $\bigcup_{n\geq 1}f^n(C(f))$ where $C(f)$ is the set of critical points of $f$. The map $f$ is called expanding (equivalently hyperbolic, or Axiom A) if $P(f)\cap J(f)=\emptyset$; equivalently, there exist constants $C>0$ and $\lambda>1$ such that some iterate $f^n$ satisfies $\|(f^n)'(z)\|_{\mathrm{sph}}\geq C\lambda^n$ uniformly for all $z\in J(f)$.

Question: Is the set of expanding maps dense in $\mathrm{Rat}_d$? Is the set of expanding maps dense in $\mathrm{Poly}_d$?
artifact.category_tag: Density of hyperbolicity in complex dynamics
artifact.status_search_result: This is the classical Fatou density-of-hyperbolicity conjecture, still open in full generality for $\mathrm{Rat}_d$ and $\mathrm{Poly}_d$ with $d\geq 2$. It has been established in important special cases: for real polynomials of any degree (Kozlovski–Shen–van Strien, 2007), for real quadratic polynomials (Lyubich; Graczyk–Świątek), and for rational maps with Cantor Julia sets (Peng–Yin–Zhai and subsequent work). The general complex case remains a central open problem in holomorphic dynamics.

status_evidence.title: Density of hyperbolicity in dimension one
status_evidence.snippet: Kozlovski, Shen, and van Strien prove density of hyperbolicity for real polynomials of arbitrary degree.
status_evidence.claim: Density of hyperbolicity proved for real one-dimensional maps; complex case remains open.

status_evidence.title: Frontiers in complex dynamics (McMullen)
status_evidence.snippet: Survey describing density of hyperbolicity as a central open problem in complex dynamics.
status_evidence.claim: The general conjecture in Rat_d and Poly_d remains open.

status_evidence.title: Density of hyperbolicity for rational maps with Cantor Julia sets
status_evidence.snippet: Each non-hyperbolic rational map with a Cantor Julia set can be approximated by hyperbolic ones of the same degree.
status_evidence.claim: Partial result: conjecture proved in the Cantor Julia set case.
